claims.text: Nonequilibrium processing can produce a homogeneous, metastable solid-solution-containing microstructure in a Mg-containing lightweight alloy.
Thermal exposure between approximately 800 °C and 1200 °C induces diffusion-controlled nucleation and growth of intermetallic phases from the metastable solid solution.
Mg-containing Mg-Ti-Zn alloys have a tendency to form multiple new phases because Ti and Zn have limited solid solubility in Mg.
The thermally generated intermetallic compounds are Ti-rich or Zn-rich.
The intermetallic compounds nucleate both at grain boundaries and within grains.
Continued thermal exposure causes the intermetallic precipitates to grow and eventually coarsen.
A fine, uniform dispersion of intermetallic precipitates can strengthen the alloy.
Fine, uniform precipitation leaves enough Mg, Ti, and Zn in the matrix to support passivating-film formation.
A Ti-rich surface film can produce passivation and high corrosion resistance in Mg-Ti-Zn alloys.
Mg, Ti, and Zn collectively form a stable protective oxide film that preserves both aqueous corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Excessive precipitate coarsening causes localized depletion of passivating elements from the matrix.
Coarsening-related compositional and microstructural heterogeneity disrupts formation of a continuous protective oxide scale.
Disruption of the protective scale by coarsening reduces corrosion resistance.
Disruption of the protective scale by coarsening reduces high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Aged samples with fine-scale precipitation will have corrosion-current densities and oxidation kinetics similar to or slightly better than the initial metastable state.
Aged samples showing advanced coarsening will exhibit significantly poorer passivation and greater corrosion and oxidation degradation than the initial metastable state.
Exposure at approximately 800–1200 °C represents the intended high-temperature service regime for the unnamed alloy.
An untreated, rapidly quenched, or low-temperature-held control will retain the initial metastable solid-solution state.
